newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Tramps of world uniting against work ethic.
newsitem.headline: Tramps of world uniting against work ethic.

text.p: Tramps from around the world arrived in the Argentine seaside resort of Mar del Plata on Monday to begin their first world conference and foment rebellion against the work ethic.
"If powerful presidents who manage huge resources can hold a summit, why can't we wanderers hold a summit too?" summit organiser Pedro Ribeira told Reuters.
The 57-year-old founder of the Free Tramps' Movement said he had summoned the world's work-shy to discuss matters like "the liberation of man from materialism" and "cheap eating on the road."

"The tramp shows total solidarity, shares his food, his knowledge, education and goods and donates his blood and organs selflessly," said Ribeira, quoting from a "tramps' manifesto" prepared by the movement.
Mar del Plata expects to play host to 300 itinerants from Argentina and abroad, including delegations from Greece, Uruguay and Canada, for a week of events culminating in a "big feed."
Those addicted to work will be admitted as observers.
Actually, many of those turning up are less drifters than dreamers, recreational wanderers who want, in Ribeira's words, to "recapture the spirit of the tramp."
He himself is a jazz musician with a comfortable Mar del Plata home. But he also has a walk to Rio de Janeiro -- more than 1,500 miles (2,400 km) -- to his credit.
The Free Tramps' Movement is rallying under a banner that depicts a down-and-outer with the traditional stick and knotted handkerchief over his shoulder.
"But we are against symbols, and we are going to burn the banner at the end of the meeting," Ribeira said. "This was just to identify ourselves when we went walking."

Many Mar del Plata shopkeepers and businessmen had been fearing an invasion of horrible hairy hoboes. But the town hall ended up providing conference facilities, including a library and a cultural centre.
